This figure is from FAA-H-8083-30A, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook: General, chapter 2 (regulations, maintenance forms, records, and publications). Its caption: "Figure 2-6. Graphic chart of FAA regulations (continued).".
Describe it for a mechanic who can't see it: say what it shows, then transcribe every label,
value, unit, part number, and note printed in it. Don't add anything that isn't in the figure.
If it shows nothing of use (a logo, a signature, a blank area), say so in one sentence.

message.content:
The figure is a flowchart titled “Recurrent Airworthiness” that maps FAA organizations, regulations, certificates, and guidance documents. It shows relationships among Flight Standards Service (AFS), the Certificate Management Office (CMO), Flight Standards District Office (FSDO), and International Field Office (IFO), with numbered regulatory parts, certificate details, and associated handbooks or forms.

This airworthiness certificate is issued pursuant to the Federal Aviation Act of 1958 and certifies that, as of the date of issuance, the aircraft to which issued has been inspected and found to conform to the type certificate therefor, to be in condition for safe operation, and has been shown to meet the requirements of the applicable comprehensive and detailed airworthiness code as provided by Annex 8 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation, except as noted herein.

NONE

6 TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Unless sooner surrendered, suspended, revoked, or a termination date is otherwise established by the Administrator, this airworthiness certificate is effective as long as the maintenance, preventative maintenance, and alterations are performed in accordance with Parts 21, 43, and 91 of the Federal Aviation Regulations, as appropriate, and the aircraft is registered in the United States.
